question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ -8 & -10 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. What are the dimensions of the eigenspaces ${V}_{-3}$ and ${V}_{-1}$ corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda =-3$ and $\lambda =-1$ of $A$, respectively?
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the characteristic equation $\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & -3-\lambda  & 0 \\ -8 & -10 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (-3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 1 \\ -8 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (-3-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(-5-\lambda )+8)=0 \\ -(\lambda +3)({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +3)=0 \\ (\lambda +3)(\lambda +3)(\lambda +1)=0 \\ (\lambda +3)^{2}(\lambda +1)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=-3$ (double root) and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1$ (simple root).

Let's now consider the eigenspaces corresponding to each eigenvector:

- First, we consider $\lambda =-1.$ Since ${V}_{-1}$ corresponds to a simple root, we obtain 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-1})=1.
$$

- Then, we consider $\lambda =-3,$ which is a repeated root of the characteristic equation. To find the dimension of ${V}_{-3},$ we row-reduce the matrix $(A-(-3)I)\text{x}=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ -8 & -10 & -5\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -8 & -10 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3.$ Therefore, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-3})=2.
$$
